 JUDGEMENT Heard on the question of admission.

2. This miscellaneous appeal is filed by the appellants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved of award dated 31/8/2010 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Multai, Distt. Betul in Claim Case no.3/2008.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Multai, Distt. Betul
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The brief facts of the case are that this appeal was filed by the claimants stating that on 7/11/2007 at about 5:55 p.m., when deceased was going by motorcycle, then the motorcycle was hit by Jeep bearing registration no.MP-48-D-0076 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") being driven rashly and negligently by the respondent no.1, resultantly, deceased sustained grievous injuries on the head due to which he died.
4.

The respondents no.1 and 2 have filed their written statement and denied the liability and have stated that at the time of accident, the vehicle was duly insured with the respondent no.3 and the deceased himself negligent and the respondent no.3 has filed the written statement and denied the claim and stated that this is a case of contributory negligent and the owner and driver have committed breach of policy.
5. After taking the evidence from both the parties, the learned claims tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.12,89,000/- in favour of the claimants.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the learned claims tribunal has committed an error in not appreciating the proper income of the deceased as he was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The learned claims tribunal has wrongly deducted the amount of pension from the income and has wrongly exonerated the insurance company from the liability.
The driver has possessed valid and effective driving license.
He was competent to drive the light motor vehicle.
It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the proper multiplier of 13 was to be applied by the learned tribunal.
The learned claims tribunal has wrongly deducted 1/3rd amount from the personal expenses.
Looking to the number of dependents the proper deduction would be 1/4th of the income.
Future prospect was also not awarded in favour of the appellants by the learned claims tribunal.
Learned claims tribunal has also not awarded the compensation for loss of consortium, estate, funeral expenses, love and affection.

Therefore, on that counts award is Smt. Padma Devi vs Shiv Shankar on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/454699/
2 requested to be enhanced appropriately.

sentences.text: 7. Per Contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondents no. 2 and 3 that the learned tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation in favour of the claimants.

8. It is pertinent to mention here that respondent no.1 did not appear before the Court despite due service while respondent no.2 has filed cross objection but that was dismissed vide order dated 1/12/2023 due to non-compliance of the Court order, and thereafter, respondent no.2 also remained absent before the Court.
9.
This miscellaneous appeal is filed on behalf of the claimants.

So far as the question of breach of policy is concerned, it is not challenged by the respondents no.1 and 2 in this case and in this regard the cross objection filed on behalf of the respondent no.2 has already been dismissed.
Therefore, the question of breach of policy is not considerable in this case.

Despite that if we considered the facts and evidence on record, it is found that on the relevant date, the offending vehicle was used for commercial purposes and material was being loaded on it and transported by it.
It is not on record that the vehicle was having the laden weight of 7500 kgs. or less.

10. In case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017)14 SCC 663, Hon'ble the Supreme Court held that holder of a licence to drive the class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in Section 10(2)(d) of the Motor Vehicle Act would be competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, having the "gross vehicle weight" does not exceed 7500 kgs.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017)14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: or a motor car or tractor or road roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kgs.
11. However, there is no evidence on record that the offending vehicle was having the weight of or less than 7500 kgs.
therefore, in absence of such evidence on record.
It cannot be said that the offending vehicle was having the weight of 7500 kgs. or less.
It was incumbent on the respondents no.1 and 2 to prove this fact but they have failed to do so.

12. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondents no.2 and 3 that vide order sheet dated 30/8/2010, the registration number of the offending vehicle was amended at the fake end of the enquiry and no proper opportunity of hearing has been granted by the learned tribunal to the non-applicants.

In this regard perusal of record shows that at the stage of final arguments on 30/8/2010, the registration number of the offending vehicle stated in para 2 and 3 of the petition,
has been amended because the registration number of offending vehicle was mistakenly stated as the registration number of damaged motorcycle but such mistake has been cured by such amendment.
Perusal of reply of the non- applicants shows that they were not misleaded by such mistake.
On the same date on 30/8/2010, they raised no objection on such amendment and thereafter they argued the matter and on the next date the impugned award has been passed by the learned tribunal.
So it does not reveal from the order sheet dated 30/8/2010 onwards that no proper opportunity of hearing was provided to the non-applicants.
Therefore, such argument is not acceptable.

sentences.text: So far as, the other contentions of the appellants are concerned the deceased was 54 years of age at the time of accident.

Therefore, the multiplier of 11 has rightly been applied by the learned tribunal, so far as the deduction is concerned, since claimants are three in numbers therefore, as per the law laid down in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 1/3rd deduction was rightly made by the learned tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Deduction of income tax amount is also not found to be illegally deducted and therefore, from the gross income of Rs.3,35,741/- after the deduction of income tax and 1/3rd of personal expenses the learned tribunal has rightly arrived at the amount of dependency of Rs.2.10 Lakh.
But in para 18 of the impugned award, learned tribunal has wrongly deducted Rs.8,000/- as family pension received by the claimants.

14. It is held in the case of Sebastiani Lakra and Others vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in (2019) 17 SCC 465 that deductions cannot be allowed from the amount of the compensation either on account of insurance, or on account of pensionary benefits or gratuity or grant of employment to a kin of the deceased.

entities.text: Sebastiani Lakra and Others vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in (2019) 17 SCC 465
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The amount received owing to the sudden death of the employee in harness shall only be deducted but since the family pension is the amount which is generally in case of death of an employee, provided to the LRs of such employee entitled to receive it and which becomes due on account of some contract or act which deceased performed in his life time.
Therefore, the amount of family pension in case of deceased as a bank employee cannot be deducted from the amount of the compensation.

15. Hence, on assessing the amount of compensation from the amount of dependency Rs.2.10 Lakh after applying the multiplier of 11 and since the learned tribunal has not awarded future prospects in terms of the law laid down in case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra)
by Hon'ble Apex Court, adding 15% towards future prospects and adding amount in the head of funeral prospects and estate loss and loss of consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such amount on assessment reached more than Rs.28 Lakh.
Since this claim petition is filed for enhancement of Rs. 15 Lakh, therefore, Rs.15 Lakh may be enhanced in favour of the claimants.
16. Therefore, Rs. 15 Lakh is enhanced in addition to the compensation already awarded in favour of the claimants on the terms and conditions stipulated by the learned tribunal in impugned award.
17. Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE m/-
